newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha trading subdued due to Easter.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha trading subdued due to Easter.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices were largely unchanged on Friday in a nearly deserted market, with most Asian traders, except for those in Japan and South Korea, away for the Easter holiday.
Open-spec naphtha for second-half May was notionally assessed at $224.50/225.50 per tonne, little changed from late Thursday's $224.50/225.00.
First-half June was bid at $224.00, but no offers emerged. It was traded at $224.00 on Thursday.
In spreads, second-half May/second-half June was assessed little changed from Thursday at plus $1.50/2.50.
The backwardation remained tight as naphtha cracker turnarounds in Japan and South Korea, scheduled for May and early June, set a bearish tone for prompt cargoes.
A petrochemical firm earlier this week bought a physical cargo to be delivered to Kawasaki, near Tokyo, in the first half of May.
It declined to comment on the price, but the deal was rumoured to have been done at around $4.00 over the mean of Japanese quotes.
